scenes.narration: Now here's the clever part. The printer has a row of tiny *heaters*. A hot dot melts the coating, dye meets acid... black.
scenes.headline: STEP 2/3: TINY *HEATERS*

scenes.narration: And your nail? Rub fast and friction makes *heat*, like rubbing your hands on a cold day. Same trick.

youtube.title: Why do receipts turn black when you scratch them? #shorts
youtube.description:
Why do receipts turn black when you scratch them? Shop receipts are thermal paper, and the receipt printer uses no ink. The paper is coated with a colourless dye and an acid, kept apart in a solid layer. The printer's row of tiny heating dots melts the coating in spots, the dye meets the acid and turns black. Rub it fast with a fingernail and friction makes enough heat to do the same thing. A hot mug can darken it too.
